subject: Web Development
title: OAuth and Single Sign-On
description: A fast breakdown of OAuth and Single Sign-On for builders.

hook.text: 'Sign in with Google' is everywhere. But how does a third party verify your identity safely?

buildup.text: OAuth lets users grant limited access to their data without sharing their password.

discovery.text: You authenticate with Google. Google gives the app a token — not your password.

twist.text: OAuth was designed for authorization, not authentication. OpenID Connect fills that gap.

climax.text: Single sign-on reduces password fatigue and centralizes security in trusted providers.

punchline.text: Let the experts handle the login.

quiz.question: What does OAuth share instead of passwords?
